H08 Stage 2: implementation, diagnostics, and V0 comparison

Visual light sensitivity and personal light exposure — author result gate

Published

August 12, 2026

NoteAccepted Stage 2 package with bounded METRIC-011 maintenance

The author accepted this Stage 2 result package before the Stage 3 and Stage 4 reports were created. On 2026-08-12, shared decision METRIC-011 normalised eight L10 participant-day round-off remnants to exact numerical zero. The bounded H08 reseal refitted only the inherited primary-dataset L10 branches and their specified diagnostics and sensitivities, then recalculated the four affected nine-member BH families. It did not rerun the full analysis or any resampling. The retained results, displayed values, diagnostic dispositions, sensitivity classifications, and scientific claims remained unchanged.

1 Hypothesis and analytical question

The signed preregistration states:

H8: Duration-, exposure-history-, and level-based metrics are associated with VLSQ-8 light sensitivity scores.

The audited question is whether participant-level VLSQ-8 scores are associated with repeated participant-day personal light-exposure metrics after adjustment for submitted site. Near-eye measurements are primary; chest measurements are complementary. Temperature and other unsupported predictors are absent.

The predefined preparation sensitivity is called the gap-timing-unaware dataset. It still passed the general 50%-per-hour and 80%-per-day coverage rules. The name means that the timing of the remaining missing observations is not used for an additional metric-specific adjustment; it does not mean that gaps, missingness, or coverage were ignored. For this one-time first explanation, the primary could be interpreted as a time-sensitive primary metric dataset because its approved preparation uses the timing of remaining missing observations where that timing is relevant. From here onward, it is called simply the primary dataset.

2 Frozen implementation contract

All 14 Stage 1 decisions are recorded as approved, and all 20 sealed inputs match their pinned SHA-256 values.

Implementation preconditions
Check Result

The accepted analysis and the bounded METRIC-011 reseal stop immediately if an approval, input pin, or invariance check fails.

2.1 METRIC-011 exact-zero reseal

The controlling METRIC-011 decision classifies floating-point remnants that are numerically zero as exact zero. Its independently verified evidence identified eight affected primary L10 means: three near-eye and five chest participant-days changed from 4.163336342344337e-17 lx to 0 lx. All samples, non-L10 values, hourly and 30-minute values, gap-timing-unaware values, V0 outputs, and the accepted exactly identified longest-period and observed-dose sensitivities were protected.

The result comparison, complete-family BH record, display-invariance record, and 33-scope reconciliation provide the machine-readable audit trail. Because no retained result or claim changed, the existing author approval remains applicable.

2.2 VLSQ-8 scoring and scaling

The participant-level predictor is complete for all 184 participants across nine sites. The stored score equals the sum of the eight ordered 1–5 item codes plus 5 for every participant. Its observed range is 13–39, its mean is 21.597826, and its participant standard deviation is 5.539840. Models use the centred raw score; practical effects compare scores separated by one such standard deviation. No within-site standardisation was applied.

VLSQ-8 score audit
Participants Sites Missing scores Missing item cells Range Mean SD Stored − item sum Verified
184 9 0 0 13–39 21.597826 5.539840 5 TRUE
The +5 scoring constant is an author-approved project convention; it is not claimed as a published standard total-score algorithm.

2.3 Exact fitted formulas

The following evaluated cell is the complete formula contract. Site uses the submitted order and explicit sum contrasts. site:Id is the participant random-intercept grouping factor; participants remain nested within site.

site_only <- stats::as.formula(
  "response_value ~ site + (1 | site:Id)"
)
additive <- stats::as.formula(
  "response_value ~ site + VLSQ8_c + (1 | site:Id)"
)
interaction <- stats::as.formula(
  "response_value ~ site * VLSQ8_c + (1 | site:Id)"
)
photoperiod_site_only <- stats::as.formula(
  "response_value ~ site + photoperiod_c + (1 | site:Id)"
)
photoperiod_additive <- stats::as.formula(
  "response_value ~ site + photoperiod_c + VLSQ8_c + (1 | site:Id)"
)
photoperiod_interaction <- stats::as.formula(
  "response_value ~ site * VLSQ8_c + photoperiod_c + (1 | site:Id)"
)
participant_site_only <- stats::as.formula(
  "participant_response ~ site"
)
participant_additive <- stats::as.formula(
  "participant_response ~ site + VLSQ8_c"
)
participant_interaction <- stats::as.formula(
  "participant_response ~ site * VLSQ8_c"
)

site_only
response_value ~ site + (1 | site:Id)
additive
response_value ~ site + VLSQ8_c + (1 | site:Id)
interaction
response_value ~ site * VLSQ8_c + (1 | site:Id)
photoperiod_site_only
response_value ~ site + photoperiod_c + (1 | site:Id)
photoperiod_additive
response_value ~ site + photoperiod_c + VLSQ8_c + (1 | site:Id)
photoperiod_interaction
response_value ~ site * VLSQ8_c + photoperiod_c + (1 | site:Id)
participant_site_only
participant_response ~ site
participant_additive
participant_response ~ site + VLSQ8_c
participant_interaction
participant_response ~ site * VLSQ8_c

The primary average association is the likelihood-ratio comparison of site_only with additive. Site heterogeneity is the separate comparison of additive with interaction. These tests answer different questions and are adjusted in different complete nine-member Benjamini–Hochberg families.

4 Primary near-eye results

No average near-eye association survived the complete nine-member BH family (0 adjusted-positive results), and no near-eye site-by-VLSQ-8 interaction survived its separate family (0 adjusted-positive results). The practical estimates below are still informative about direction and uncertainty; they are not evidence that every true effect is exactly null.

Raw p-values compare site-only with additive models. BH adjustment is across all nine metrics. Significant adjusted p-values would be bold; none is bold.

The melEDI-dose estimate was a ratio of 0.846 per VLSQ-8 SD (95% CI 0.716–0.999), while its likelihood-ratio raw p-value was 0.051 and its BH-adjusted p-value was 0.160. The Wald interval and likelihood-ratio test use different inferential constructions; the complete family decision is therefore inconclusive, not statistically significant. The same family qualification applies to all unadjusted patterns.

The main limitations are specific:

  • Darkest 10 h mean showed increasing residual spread with fitted values (absolute-residual versus fitted Spearman correlations 0.341 near eye and 0.349 chest). Its direction and intervals should therefore be read with extra caution.
  • Time below 1 lx melEDI during sleep contained four observed exact zeros at each placement, whereas the fitted compound-Poisson model assigned an extremely small expected zero count. This is a conspicuous relative discrepancy but only four rows in each large fitted frame. The model is retained under the approved common-family gate, with the zero-mass mismatch stated explicitly.
  • The corrected melEDI-dose fits passed the main numerical checks, but the correction is timing-dependent and is therefore interpreted alongside the exact common-sample dataset and observed-dose sensitivities below.

10.2 Exactly identified longest period and observed dose

The primary longest-period metric is an observed lower bound. Requiring exact identification reduced the available sample and did not yield a precise association: near eye 0.958× (95% CI 0.856–1.072) and chest 0.939× (95% CI 0.855–1.032). On the exactly paired sample, estimates were 0.943× near eye and 0.952× chest, with both intervals crossing one.

The observed-dose comparison holds the corrected-dose fitted sample fixed and replaces the value with uncorrected observed dose. It is descriptive. The all-available near-eye estimate was 0.842× (95% CI 0.713–0.995), but the paired near-eye interval crossed one; the chest all-available interval also reached one. These sensitivities do not override the primary BH family.

10.3 Deferred upstream-dependent scenarios

Approved Rule B/Rule C daily-denominator variants and the all-zero-inclusive scenario are not H08-ready direct inputs. They remain deferred rather than being approximated within H08. Stage 2 does not require an upstream change request because the available, hash-verified sensitivity battery addresses the current result gate. If the author makes those scenarios mandatory before Stage 3, H08 will write audit/handoffs/H08_shared_change_request.md and stop for the upstream producer.

12 V0 reconstruction and reconciliation

V0 is reproducible from the archived RData files and rendered outputs. It used chest as the main placement, near eye as a robustness repeat, default treatment coding, (1 | Id), and a joint score-plus-site-interaction block as its association test. It then called p.adjust() on one scalar at a time with n = 9. That scalar operation reproduces the displayed strings but is not a nine-member FDR adjustment. A consistent vector BH calculation is retained in the audit artifact for comparison.

The tests are not numerically interchangeable: V0 tests the joint score-plus-interaction block, whereas the audited average test adds one centred score slope after site. No audited BH-adjusted conclusion is positive.

The audited implementation therefore does not convert a V0 positive result into a negative one. Rather, it replaces a nonstandard display adjustment and a differently defined joint test with the approved average-slope and heterogeneity families. The defensible Stage 2 conclusion is that the observed data do not provide multiplicity-adjusted evidence of an association between VLSQ-8 score and any of the nine near-eye metrics; chest and the sensitivity battery do not materially strengthen that evidence. Several estimates lean toward less bright-light exposure at higher scores, but their family-adjusted evidence and site stability are inconclusive. These are associations, not physiological responses or health effects.

13 Reproducibility and artifact map

The Stage 2 runner fitted all approved models in R 4.6.1, wrote frozen model frames and bundles, and exported tables, diagnostics, figures, source data, and manifests. It used maintained reformulas formula helpers. The later METRIC-011 script performed only the bounded L10 maintenance described above and preserved all other model objects. Neither run used bootstrap, simulation, or other resampling, so the pilot-runtime gate was not triggered.

14 Stage 2 package status

ImportantAccepted result package

The author accepted the following as one Stage 2 result package:

  1. Accept the eight complete nine-member BH families and the conclusion that none has an adjusted p-value below 0.05.
  2. Accept the primary near-eye and complementary chest practical estimates, 95% Wald confidence intervals, exact fitted samples, and separate site-heterogeneity interpretation.
  3. Accept the retained response families with explicit limitations for Darkest 10 h mean residual spread, sleep-below-1-lx zero mass, and the timing-dependent corrected dose.
  4. Accept the leave-one-site-out interpretation: some estimates are site-sensitive, no site is removed, and the overall result remains inconclusive.
  5. Accept the exact paired-placement display without pooling or equivalence claims and without an additional p-value screen.
  6. Accept the gap-timing-unaware, photoperiod, participant-summary, exactly-identified-longest-period, and observed-dose sensitivity interpretations.
  7. Accept the V0 reconstruction and the explanation that V0 and the audited model test different null hypotheses and use different multiplicity procedures.
  8. Accept the plain-language claim boundary: no multiplicity-adjusted evidence for an H08 association, with uncertain directional patterns and no causal, physiological, or health-effect claim.

Stage 3 and Stage 4 were subsequently completed and accepted. The Stage 3 notebook includes the REPORT-012 Results in brief callout directly after the hypothesis and analytical question. METRIC-011 did not alter that callout or any of the multiplicity, uncertainty, chest, or sensitivity qualifications.
